hero.title: Five Principles of Buddhism: Panchsheel
hero.description: An analysis of the foundational ethical code (Pancha-sila) governing the conduct of Buddhist lay practitioners.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Developed in the Gangetic plain (Magadha/Kosala).
  • Spread via trade routes to Taxila and Ujjain.

Personalities

  • Gautama Buddha (Proponent).
  • Ananda (Disseminator).
  • Ashoka (State Patron).

The Five Principles (Pancha-sila) Mindmap

  • 1. Panatipata Veramani: Abstaining from killing living beings (Ahimsa).
  • 2. Adinnadana Veramani: Abstaining from taking what is not given (Non-stealing).
  • 3. Kamesu Micchacara Veramani: Abstaining from sexual misconduct.
  • 4. Musavada Veramani: Abstaining from false speech.
  • 5. Surameraya Majja Pamadatthana Veramani: Abstaining from intoxicants.
PrincipleSanskrit ConceptObjective
1AhimsaRespect for all life
2AsteyaIntegrity in trade/property
3Brahmacharya/SilaSensory restraint
4SatyaCommitment to truth
5AppamadaMindfulness

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Prelims
mnemonics.description: Remember the 5 Sila (vows) using the acronym: S.T.A.L.I

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Do not confuse Panchsheel of Buddhism with the 1954 Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (India-China).
Pancha-sila are strictly moral precepts for laypeople; monastics follow the 'Dasa-sila' or 10 precepts.
